title: Whole Sea Bass Baked in a Salt Crust with Lemon and Herbs
summary: A whole sea bass is packed inside a thick, egg-white-bound salt crust and baked so it steams gently in its own juices, then cracked open at the table for moist, delicately seasoned flesh.
equipment: heavy spoon or rolling pin, to crack the crust

ingredients.item: whole sea bass or sea bream, about 650 g each, scaled and gutted
coarse sea salt or kosher salt, for the crust

ingredients.note: about 100 g; for the crust only, not eaten

steps.title: Heat the Oven
steps.text: Set the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C) and line the large tray with baking paper. Starting from a fully hot oven helps the thick salt crust heat through evenly in good time.

steps.title: Stuff the Cavities
steps.text: Rinse the sea bass inside and out under cold water and pat completely dry. Fill each cavity with half the lemon slices, garlic, thyme, rosemary and parsley. These aromatics perfume the flesh gently as the fish steams inside its crust.

steps.title: Mix the Salt Crust
steps.text: Combine the salt, egg whites and water by hand in a large bowl until the mixture feels like damp sand and holds together when squeezed, adding a little more water if it still crumbles. The egg white binds the crystals into a solid shell that hardens around the fish as it bakes.

steps.title: Pack the Fish
steps.text: Spread about a third of the salt mixture into two beds on the tray, each a little longer than a fish and about 1cm thick, then lay a fish on each bed. Press the rest of the salt all over to seal them completely in a 1cm layer, leaving just the heads and tails peeking out. Patch any gaps carefully, since they let steam escape and let too much salt reach the flesh.

steps.title: Bake and Check
steps.text: Bake for 25-30 minutes, then push a probe thermometer through the crust into the thickest part of the back, just behind the head, checking it reads at least 63°C. If it isn't there yet, bake for a further 5 minutes and test again. The hardened crust traps steam so thoroughly that the fish cooks in its own juices rather than drying in the oven's heat.

steps.title: Rest the Fish
steps.text: Leave the fish to rest on the tray for 5 minutes once out of the oven. This brief pause lets the juices inside settle back through the flesh before you break into the crust.

steps.title: Char the Lemon
steps.text: While the fish rests, cook the lemon halves cut side down in the dry small pan over medium-high heat for 2-3 minutes until browned. Charring mellows their sharpness into a gentler contrast for the fish.

steps.title: Crack and Serve
steps.text: Tap the crust all over with the back of a heavy spoon and lift it off in large pieces, then brush away loose salt and peel off and discard the top skin, which carries too much salt to eat. Lift the top fillet off the bone in pieces, remove the backbone, then lift out the lower fillet, leaving the bottom skin behind, checking carefully for stray bones. Drizzle with olive oil, grind over pepper and serve with the charred lemon.

tips: Pack the salt crust at an even 1cm thickness all over with no gaps, or steam will escape and the flesh can end up oversalted in patches.
Mix the salt to a damp-sand consistency; too wet and it won't hold its shape, too dry and it won't seal properly.
Always discard the salt-soaked top skin before serving, since it carries far too much salt to eat.
Check the internal temperature with a probe through the thickest part of the back rather than relying on time alone, as crust thickness can vary.
storage: Best eaten the day it's baked, since the crust is discarded once cracked and the flesh doesn't hold up well cold. Any leftover fillet meat can be refrigerated in a sealed container for up to 1 day and reheated gently until piping hot (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
